paper_title: The Parameterized Complexity Of Extending Stack Layouts
classifications: Theory of computation → Fixed parameter tractability
Mathematics of computing → Graphs and surfaces
statement: A further natural and promising direction for future work is to consider generalizing the presented techniques to other types of linear layouts, such as queue layouts. Finally, future work could also investigate the following generalized notion of extending linear layouts: Given a graph G, the spine order for some subset of its vertices and the page assignment for some subset of its edges, does there exist a linear layout of G that extends both simultaneously?
context: ▶ Theorem 8.1 (★). Let I = (ℓ, G, H, ⟨≺, σ⟩) be an instance of SLE where G[Vadd ] is an independent set. We can find an ℓ-page stack layout of G that extends ⟨≺, σ⟩ or report that 2 none exists in O(ℓmadd · nadd ! · madd nadd · (madd |I| )) time. A further natural and promising direction for future work is to consider generalizing the presented techniques to other types of linear layouts, such as queue layouts. Finally, future work could also investigate the following generalized notion of extending linear layouts: Given a graph G, the spine order for some subset of its vertices and the page assignment for some subset of its edges, does there exist a linear layout of G that extends both simultaneously?
